content_voiceover: This slide presents another treatment algorithm for higher risk myelofibrosis, published in Blood in October 2024, organized around splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms as the entry point. If the patient has no cytopenias, first line therapy is ruxolitinib, and the dose is tailored to the platelet count, 20 milligrams twice daily if platelets exceed 200, 15 milligrams twice daily for platelets between 100 and 200, and just 5 milligrams twice daily for platelets between 50 and 100. If platelets are under 50, ruxolitinib is skipped altogether in favor of pacritinib. On first line ruxolitinib, if the patient develops worsening splenomegaly or symptoms without cytopenias, the next step is fedratinib; if cytopenias develop instead, the pathway moves to momelotinib or pacritinib, chosen again by anemia and platelet status. Separately, if the presenting problem includes anemia with transfusion dependence right from the start, momelotinib is the first line choice, and if it fails, the second line choice bifurcates by platelet count into ruxolitinib or fedratinib for higher platelets, or pacritinib territory for lower platelets. On the right side of the diagram, if the primary problem is anemia plus thrombocytopenia with platelets 25 or above, momelotinib is again favored, while pacritinib is favored if platelets are below 50. The unifying concept is that drug selection in myelofibrosis is really a three way negotiation between spleen and symptom burden, platelet count, and anemia or transfusion dependence, and this diagram is a nice practical companion to the Taiwan algorithm from the previous slide.
keypoints: Ruxolitinib dosing is platelet tiered, 20mg BID over 200, down to 5mg BID for 50 to 100
Platelets under 50 at baseline, skip ruxolitinib, start pacritinib
Anemia with transfusion dependence, momelotinib preferred first line
Second line after ruxolitinib failure depends on cytopenias vs spleen or symptom progression
Drug choice balances spleen response, platelet count, and anemia
keypoint_voiceover: Think of drug selection in MF as balancing three variables, spleen and symptom burden, platelet count, and anemia. Ruxolitinib dosing scales down as platelets drop, from 20 milligrams twice daily above 200,000 to 5 milligrams twice daily between 50 and 100,000. Below 50,000 platelets, skip straight to pacritinib. If transfusion dependent anemia dominates the picture, momelotinib is the first choice, both up front and after ruxolitinib failure.
